expansion:
A. Secondary optic atrophy is correct. The key feature is optic atrophy following a period of disc swelling from papilledema: chronic raised intracranial pressure first produces papilledema, then the previously swollen disc becomes pale, flat and atrophic. This is secondary optic atrophy (not taken from the course material). The lecture identifies papilledema with “↑ ICP” and marked disc elevation, “+ + +” (L21, slide 8). Its optic-atrophy slide shows the Secondary disc as “DIRTY GREY-WHITE,” with “INDISTINCT AND BLURRED” margins and hazy peripapillary retina, described as “the residue of the swelling that preceded the atrophy” (L21, slide 14). This fits the sequence in the stem.

B. Primary optic atrophy is wrong because it is not the atrophy that follows visible disc oedema. It classically follows damage to the optic nerve without prior intraocular disc swelling, leaving a pale disc with sharply defined margins (not taken from the course material). The lecture’s Primary photograph is a “CHALKY WHITE disc” with margins that are “CLEARLY DEFINED AND SHARP” and a normal surrounding retina (L21, slide 14), unlike the post-papilledema scenario.

C. Consecutive optic atrophy is wrong because it follows retinal disease, rather than prolonged papilledema or raised intracranial pressure (not taken from the course material). The lecture depicts it as a “WAXY YELLOW disc” with “MARKEDLY ATTENUATED” vessels and an abnormal background retina in which “the retinal disease that caused the atrophy is visible” (L21, slide 14).

D. Glaucomatous optic atrophy is wrong because it results from glaucomatous optic neuropathy, characteristically with pathological cupping, not from papilledema (not taken from the course material). The lecture shows a “deep and large” cup occupying most of the disc, with pallor “CONFINED TO THE CUP” (L21, slide 14).

The lecture names all four types but does not explicitly define their causes; the causal classification above is therefore not taken from the course material.
objective: Identify secondary optic atrophy as optic disc pallor and atrophy that follows prolonged papilledema.
